headline: Hot September CPI (3.7% headline, core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected) sends semis down 4.3% and BTC to $80.6K (-3.4% 24h), below the $81.7K ETF cost basis; hl-cycles flips to mild risk-off
tldr: Regime: hl-cycles flipped from mild risk-on to mild risk-off (33% BTC, since Oct 12; 2 of 6 stress conditions on). Main change: the Oct 14 CPI beat lifted October hike odds from about 20% to roughly 44-46% (sources differ), the S&P fell 1.1% to 7,718.94 and BTC and ETH fell 3.4% and 6.1% on 24h. Main disagreement: BTC OI did not fall ($3.20B, z30 +0.9) and funding sits at its baseline, so longs have not been flushed, while the stablecoin series dropped to z30 -3.7. Next catalysts: Russia/Iran sanctions implementation Oct 18 (no fresh coverage found), FOMC Oct 27-28. Not financial advice.

domains.summary: September CPI (Oct 14) printed 3.7% y/y headline against a 3.6% forecast in one source, with core +0.3% m/m against 0.2% expected; reports tie the energy-driven inflation to Middle East supply disruption. Reported October 28 hike odds rose to roughly 44-46% from about 20% (sources range from 44% to 50%; December odds are above 50% in one source and above 95% in another, so we treat them as low-confidence). Rates: 10Y 5.21%, 2Y 4.79%, 30Y 5.56% (Oct 13, FRED; Oct 14 not yet printed). 2s10s narrowed to +37bp on Oct 14 from +42bp, but with the 10Y and 2Y both near flat since Oct 6 we cannot name a steepener or flattener driver until Oct 14 yields print. Oil is stale in FRED: Brent $125.44 and WTI $96.24 on Oct 6, so the oil input is unverified for the last six sessions. Dollar index 121.60 (Oct 9). We read the stance as restrictive, and hl-cycles Macro lens is 30 (Restrictive, 7d -3.9). What would change the read: a December hike probability falling back below 50% or Brent falling under $100.

Oct 14 cash close (FRED/Yahoo): S&P 500 7,718.94 (-1.1%, -0.98% over 5 sessions per SPY), Nasdaq Comp 26,692.87 (-1.9%), Dow 51,621.48 (-0.1%). Semis led the loss: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 4.3%, its sixth straight decline, and SMH is -9.7% over 5 sessions (NVDA -6.8%). QQQ is -3.8% and IWM -2.3% over 5 sessions. VIX (Yahoo) jumped 10.5% on the day to 16.87 (FRED's Oct 13 print was 15.27). Calm volatility sitting on a 5.2% 10Y was the part we flagged last run; the CPI print is the first test, and VIX at 16.9 says the market is treating it as a tech-specific repricing and not a broad de-risking (low-confidence). What would change the read: VIX above 20 or the S&P closing below 7,600. No put/call ratio found.

Price/OI/funding: BTC -3.4% 24h to $80,580 (HL mark) and ETH -6.1% to $2,350, while BTC OI barely moved ($3.20B app series vs $3.15B previous, z30 +0.9) and funding sits at the HL baseline (1.25e-5/h, z30 +1.0). Price down with OI holding and flat funding means the sell-off came from spot and new shorts offsetting longs, not a long flush; ETH OI is lower ($2.69B, z30 -1.7), so ETH is deleveraging more than BTC. HL total OI $11.72B (z30 -0.9), funding skew z30 +1.0: crowding is low, and no washout is confirmed because BTC OI has not dropped. Unusual: BTC dominance 59.8% (z30 +2.8, from 59.2%) shows alts underperforming; the stablecoin series fell to $309.9B (-0.8% day, z30 -3.7; DefiLlama's chart, a different aggregate, shows $305.5B, -0.6% 7d, +0.6% 30d), so the supply signal is a drain, not new dry powder. Fear & Greed 62 (flat, z30 -0.0) and DVOL 38.5 (z30 +1.9) have not caught up with the move. BTC moved with Nasdaq/semis this run (QQQ -2.0% on the day), so it reads macro-driven, in contrast to last run. What would change the read: BTC OI falling below $3.0B with F&G under 50 would make it a washout; OI rising with funding z30 above +2 would mean shorts are being squeezed or leverage is rebuilding.

Oct 14 closes (Yahoo), day change and 5-session change: NVDA $221.30 (-3.2%, -6.8%), META $737.54 (-3.3%, +2.3%), MSFT $533.69 (-1.8%, +0.7%), GOOGL $347.64 (-1.7%, -0.8%), AMZN $254.08 (-1.7%, -2.3%), AAPL $342.96 (+0.5%, +1.9%). SMH $564.74 fell 4.0% on the day and 9.7% over 5 sessions. Dispersion has narrowed in the wrong direction: last run platforms held while semis fell, and on Oct 14 five of six names fell; only AAPL gained. Reports of China's CXMT progress on memory chips added a stock-specific leg to the semis drop. SMH is -4.4% since the Oct 12 close ($590.99), just short of the -5% trigger set last run. What would change the read: SMH closing back above its Oct 12 level ($590.99). No earnings dates for the six were verified this run.

Live searches this run (Oct 15) found no new coverage dated this week of the Oct 18 Russia/Iran sanctions-act implementation or of Hormuz; the newest item we can cite for that is last run's (late September), so the Oct 18 date is carried as unverified. The Oct 14 CPI coverage ties the energy-driven inflation to Middle East supply disruption, which keeps oil in play as the main geopolitical transmission into rates. Linkage: with Brent last verified at $125 (Oct 6, FRED), an actual tariff on a top oil importer would plausibly add to inflation ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC; a waiver would likely remove that. What would change the read: a dated announcement of tariffs or a waiver before Oct 18.

thesis.observe: BTC $80,580 (HL mark, -3.4% 24h) and ETH $2,350 (-6.1%); BTC OI $3.20B (z30 +0.9), HL total OI $11.72B (z30 -0.9), BTC funding +0.00125%/h (z30 +1.0); BTC dominance 59.8% (z30 +2.8); stablecoin series $309.9B (z30 -3.7); F&G 62, DVOL 38.5. hl-cycles: mild risk-off since Oct 12, Compass 46 (Neutral), Macro 30 (Restrictive), ETF cost basis $81.7K, True Market Mean $79.2K (BTC about 1.7% above on the HL mark), STH cost basis $74.3K. Sep CPI 3.7% y/y, core +0.3% m/m; S&P 7,718.94, SMH -9.7% over 5 sessions, VIX 16.87, 10Y 5.21% (Oct 13).
thesis.infer: Positioning: price down, OI flat-to-up and funding at baseline means longs have not been flushed and shorts are not paying to press, so the move reads as macro-driven spot selling after CPI rather than a leverage washout. Disagreement: Fear & Greed (62) and DVOL (38.5) still price a calm tape while the stablecoin series is at z30 -3.7, hl-cycles has turned risk-off and the Macro lens is Restrictive. Consensus is pricing roughly even odds of an October hike and a likely December hike; we read the risk as skewing hawkish into Oct 27-28 unless oil falls.
thesis.forecast: Base case (we lean here, low-confidence): BTC trades between the True Market Mean ($79.2K) and the ETF cost basis ($81.7K) while OI stays near $3.2B, with hl-cycles confirming risk-on only on a daily close above $81.7K with realized cap growing. Tail case (low-confidence): a daily close below $79.2K, which hl-cycles lists as invalidating, would put the STH cost basis ($74.3K, about 8% below) in play. Second tail case (low-confidence): a Fed or oil de-escalation reverses the hike pricing, with BTC reclaiming $81.7K and the stablecoin series recovering above $312B. Consensus is pricing a slower pace of hikes than the CPI beat implies; we read the risk as the December path.
thesis.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Market intelligence only — a reasoned read of public data, not a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

risks: Daily BTC close below $79.2K (True Market Mean, hl-cycles invalidation level)
BTC OI above $3.5B with BTC funding z30 above +2 while price stays under $81.7K (leverage building into weakness)
SMH closing below $530 (about 6% below Oct 14) before Oct 21
VIX closing above 20 before the Oct 27-28 FOMC
